title: Associated-point criterion for a regular section of an invertible sheaf
statement: Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth], let $L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module], and let $s\in\Gamma(X,L)$. Write $\operatorname{Ass}(X)$ for the associated points [def-sc-associated-points], namely points $x$ whose local ring has maximal ideal equal to the annihilator of some element. Then the following conditions are equivalent: (i) for every $x\in\operatorname{Ass}(X)$ the image of $s_x$ in $L_x/\mathfrak m_xL_x$ is nonzero; (ii) for every affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$ and every trivialization $L|_U=A^{\sim}e$, writing $s|_U=ae$ with $a\in A$, the map $A\to A$, $b\mapsto ab$, is injective. Here $\mathfrak m_x$ is the maximal ideal of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ and the quotient is the fibre over the residue field [def-weil-residue-field]. Condition (ii) is the regular-section condition. The empty scheme is allowed, and no reducedness, irreducibility or quasi-compactness is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0AYL, lemma-regular-section-associated-points; the affine coefficient formulation of regularity is lemma-regular-section-structure-sheaf, Tag 01WZ.

proof.text: Fix an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$ with a frame $e$ of $L|_U$, and write $s|_U=ae$. The ring $A$ is Noetherian by [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth]. For $x\in U$ corresponding to $\mathfrak p\subset A$, [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] identifies the germ map with $A\to A_{\mathfrak p}$. Its maximal ideal is $\mathfrak pA_{\mathfrak p}$ by [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. These identifications concern the ambient stalk $\mathcal O_{X,x}$, so they require no separate assertion about associated points under open restriction.

proof.text: The frame identifies $L_x$ with $A_{\mathfrak p}e_x$, and hence its fibre with $(A_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak pA_{\mathfrak p})e_x$ by [def-sc-invertible-module] and [def-weil-residue-field]. The fibre image of $s_x$ is the class of $a/1$ times the basis vector. It is nonzero exactly when $a\notin\mathfrak p$: if $a\in\mathfrak p$ its class is zero, while if $a\notin\mathfrak p$, $a/1$ is a unit in the local ring [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] and has nonzero image in its residue field. This also proves that nonvanishing is independent of the frame.

proof.text: Assume (i). For any affine trivialization in step 1, each associated prime $\mathfrak p$ of $A$ corresponds by step 2 to an associated point of $X$ in $U$. Step 3 and (i) give $a\notin\mathfrak p$ for every such prime. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-zerodivisors-union-associated-primes] to the Noetherian ring $A$ to conclude that $ab=0$ implies $b=0$. If $ab=ac$, then $a(b-c)=0$, so $b=c$. Thus multiplication by $a$ is injective in every affine trivialization, proving (ii).

source.place: Tag 0AYL, lemma-regular-section-associated-points, hint; algebra.tex Tag 00LD, lemma-ass-zero-divisors, with M = R

proof.text: Assume (ii), and let $x\in\operatorname{Ass}(X)$. Local rank-one freeness [def-sc-invertible-module] gives an open neighbourhood with a frame; [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis] refines it to an affine neighbourhood $U$ of $x$ with that frame. For its coefficient $a$, (ii) says that $ab=0$ forces $b=0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-zerodivisors-union-associated-primes], $a$ lies in no associated prime of $A$. The prime corresponding to $x$ is associated by step 2, so step 3 proves that $s_x$ has nonzero fibre image. This is (i). No global frame or finite affine cover is needed.

source.place: Tag 0AYL, lemma-regular-section-associated-points, affine trivialization; schemes.tex Tag 01IT, lemma-basis-affine-opens; algebra.tex Tag 00LD, lemma-ass-zero-divisors

proof.text: Finally, (ii) is equivalent to injectivity of $\mathcal O_X\to L$, $b\mapsto bs$, the regular-section definition preceding Tag 01WZ. If this sheaf map is injective, its component over a trivializing affine $U$ is precisely multiplication by $a$. Conversely, for a kernel section over any open $W$, cover $W$ by affine trivializing opens using [def-sc-invertible-module] and [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]; (ii) kills its restriction to each member, and the sheaf uniqueness axiom kills the section. Kernels are sectionwise by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For $X=\varnothing$, there are no associated points; every section ring on its only open is the zero ring, and multiplication on it is injective. Both conditions therefore hold, as claimed.
